eventMetadata.context_description: Recent short-range forecasts from agencies including the Met Office and BBC place Warsaw's August 11 high at 22–23 °C amid sunny intervals, decreasing cloud cover, and moderate northwesterly winds that limit daytime heating. This tight clustering around the seasonal average of roughly 23–24 °C, combined with typical model spread of 1–2 °C from variations in boundary-layer moisture and insolation, explains why traders assign nearly equal implied probabilities to the two leading outcomes. Northwesterly flow advecting cooler maritime air and modest afternoon mixing suppress stronger warming, while any reduction in cloud cover or lighter winds could push readings toward 24 °C. Resolution hinges on official IMGW station measurements of the daily maximum.
